subject: Dedicated capacity options and ramping alternatives for ScalerPath
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@scalerpath.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity options for ScalerPath — initial ask

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. To follow up from our side: ScalerPath is preparing to move latency-sensitive generation (2k token context, mostly open-model LlamaX-70B family variants) to a dedicated capacity arrangement. We expect steady-state traffic that looks like: 250 qps of short chat completions during peak windows (15–30s tails for multi-turn), with batchy nightly bulk embeddings/finetune inference jobs.

Key asks we want you to propose for the commercial packet:
- Recommended cluster sizing (min GPUs / typical operating GPUs) and a conservative activation path for 6 months.
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs (what we must commit to) vs. burst capacity options.
- Warm-up and pre-warming approach so we don’t see throughput cliffs day 1.
- Suggested SLA and guardrails for tail latency at 95/99.
- Example pricing or range attached to each option so our finance team can model TCO.

Could you send 2–3 alternative reservation structures we can review with our CTO and procurement? We’re targeting an initial contract decision by end of August.

Appreciate it — simple slides or a short spreadsheet are fine.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering
ScalerPath

Alicia —

Thanks — attached is a short packet that lays out three distinct reservation profiles and an activation cadence we typically see work well for customers with your traffic mix. High level here:

1) Pilot Lane (conservative)
- Baseline commit: 8 GPUs (A100-class equiv)
- Typical operating: 8–12 GPUs (autoscale up to 16 for bursts)
- Ramp: 0–8 over 4 weeks; optional second tranche to 16 at month 3 if throughput growth materializes
- Warm-up: 48–72 hours of pre-warm with KV cache seeding + 25% warm-start credits
- Pricing: reserved monthly baseline + usage for burst hours; example ballpark: $Xk–$Yk/month (spreadsheet attached)

2) Production Lane (recommended for initial production)
- Baseline commit: 24 GPUs
- Typical operating: 24–36 GPUs (elastic burst to 48)
- Ramp: 8 -> 24 over 6 weeks, with staged activation windows and delivery SLA
- Warm-up: 5 days of rolling pre-warm + end-to-end smoke tests; KV pre-seeding for persistent sessions
- Pricing: blended reserved rate, lower unit cost; see sheet for modeled 12-month TCO

3) Elastic Committed (throughput+cost optimization)
- Baseline commit: 48 GPUs (min-guarantee)
- Typical operating: 48–80 GPUs (burst lanes and geo-fallback)
- Ramp: staged (month 1: 24, month 2: 40, month 4: 48) — we can compress or extend the cadence
- Warm-up: two-week gradual activation with spike simulation and fallback policies
- Pricing: largest volume discounts, options for step-downs after defined milestones

Notes on guarantees and safety nets:
- Min GPUs = hard reservation for capacity planning and scheduling; burst capacity is best-effort but can be contractually backed via reserved buffer pools (we can allocate a small hot-standby pool for your account).
- Tail latency depends on model variant and sequence length. For the LlamaX-70B family we typically target 95th < 300ms and 99th < 1.2s under Production Lane sizing with KV cache effective. We can tighten with larger clusters or more aggressive batching.

I attached: redwood_scalerpath_dedicated_options_v1.pdf and a simple spreadsheet (v1) with modeled GPU-hours.

If helpful I’ll loop Karthik for implementation constraints and Marissa on commercial structuring.

Cheers,
Priyom Das

From: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options for ScalerPath — implementation notes

Looping in a few technical constraints we should surface to the customer before they sign:

- Model sharding and KV placement: for >16 GPUs we recommend an even kv-partition layout; otherwise tails and memory pressure will increase. That pushes our practical minimum for stable multi-turn throughput to ~12 GPUs if they expect sustained 250 qps bursts.
- Cold-start mitigations: recommend a 72h KV seeding window for conversation-heavy workloads and an additional 48h of background prefetch for top-100 prompt families.
- Batching policy: for LlamaX-70B, prioritize latency SLOs with small dynamic batches (8–16 examples) rather than large fixed batches; this avoids 95/99 tail spikes while preserving throughput.
- Storage I/O and embeddings jobs: separate the nightly heavy batch jobs to a non-latency lane to avoid interference (we can reserve dedicated slots or throttle during peak).

Commercial implication: if ScalerPath wants hard burst guarantees, we should propose a small reserved buffer (6–12 GPUs) that sits idle except for peak — higher committed spend but predictable capacity.

I’ll prepare a short implementation appendix for the v2 packet (node sizing, OS image, kernel/ops compatibility notes).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Thanks — good detail. A couple of clarifying points before we take this to procurement:

- On the Pilot Lane: 8 GPUs seems low for our stated peak qps unless the burst buffer is guaranteed. Can you confirm whether the burst pool can be reserved and priced?
- Pricing: can you provide a per-GPU-month committed number and a separate hourly burst rate we can plug into our cost model? The spreadsheet helped but procurement wants unit rates.
- Ramp cadence: we’d prefer a slower ramp (month 1 -> 10 GPUs, month 2 -> 18 GPUs, month 4 -> 24 GPUs) to match our rolling feature launches; can you update the plan accordingly?
- DocuSign: sendable packet would be great — we want the commercial terms and the SLA appendix to be sign-ready.

Also cc’d our infra lead; they asked whether Redwood will perform the initial KV seeding or if we need to export session histories for you to pre-warm.

Regards,
Alicia
